clue.text: It’s most important you and I gain 81 stone

indicators.note: to gain something is to take it in, so the first pair of words acquires the number inside

blocks.note: the first person plural pronoun
read as eight and one, with one written as the Roman numeral I
ST is the abbreviation for the stone weight

explanation.surface: A weight-watcher boasts that the two of them putting on 81 stone is the big news.
explanation.walkthrough: 81 is split into its digits, eight and one. A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carrying the greatest weight in an argument is the most significant, so 'weightiest' is a synonym for most important.

clue.text: During fitting, queen’s certain to lose small opening

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so the royal letters go within the word for fitting
to lose something is to be left without it, so the word for certain sheds the size abbreviation

blocks.note: apt means suitable or fitting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
sure means certain
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A dressmaker notes that the queen is bound to slim down during her fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small opening' reads as one phrase, but small belongs to the wordplay as the clothing-size letter and the definition is just the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, as in a camera lens, so it is a synonym for an opening.

clue.text: Settlers kennel 10 dogs

indicators.note: to kennel an animal is to shut it inside, so the settlers enclose the number

blocks.note: the Boers were Dutch settlers in southern Africa
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Pioneering settlers house ten dogs in kennels.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 looks like a reference to another clue, but it is simply the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are a breed of German dog with a square muzzle, so they are dogs.

clue.text: Where to find roses in county

blocks.note: first meaning: garden plots where flowers grow
second meaning: the short form of Bedfordshire

explanation.surface: A gardener asks where in the county roses can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire, often shortened in writing, is an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses are planted in flower beds, and the abbreviation for Bedfordshire is the same four letters.

clue.text: One reviewing moon, star and limits of double quasar

definitions.text: One reviewing moon, star and limits of double quasar

indicators.note: a limit is a word's end point, so only the closing letter of each of the last two words is kept
to re-view things is to look at them afresh in another arrangement, so the gathered letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of double
the final letter of quasar

explanation.surface: A scientist surveys the night sky: a moon, a star and a double quasar.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the word and describes the person, who studies moons, stars and quasars.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer studies celestial bodies such as moons, stars and quasars, so the whole clue paints one.

clue.text: More glamorous bird, perhaps circling tree

indicators.note: circling something means going all round it, so the bird word wraps around the tree

blocks.note: a bird is one example of something that flies
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A showier bird circles a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that a bird is only one kind of flier.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashy means showy or ostentatious, so the comparative form means more glamorous.

clue.text: Game of golf described by newly-wed

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the newly-wed encircles the letter

blocks.note: Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G
a bride is a woman just married

explanation.surface: A round of golf is recounted by a just-married woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game of golf' looks like one phrase, but the game is the definition and golf is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships.

clue.text: Pastry delivered for loafer?

definitions.note: a loafer is one example of the answer, hence the question mark

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the pastry word is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: choux is the light pastry used for eclairs and profiteroles

explanation.surface: A baker's delivery of pastry goes to an idle layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loafer' suggests an idler, a fair surface link to bread; here it is the slip-on footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is a slip-on leather item of footwear, one example of the general category.

clue.text: Penny wears fake Rolexes to impress Romeo, Cook and Drake?

definitions.note: plural examples, hence the question mark

indicators.note: something worn is put on around you, so the coin letter sits within the other letters
fake goods are not what they seem, so these letters are reworked into another order
impressing something presses it into a surface, so the phonetic letter is pressed in among the watches before they are reworked

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
taken as written
Romeo is the NATO alphabet word for R

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny wears counterfeit watches to win over a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain James Cook and Sir Francis Drake were famous English voyagers, which is why the definition needs a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cook charted the Pacific and Drake sailed round the world, so both are examples of famous voyagers of discovery.

clue.text: Demo initially lost 950 in wood

indicators.note: the opening Roman numeral must shed 950 in value, turning one thousand into fifty

blocks.note: a march is a demonstration through the streets

explanation.surface: A protest at first loses 950 people in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Roman 1,000 and L is 50, so taking 950 from the first letter swaps M for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose timber is a familiar building material, so it is a type of wood.

clue.text: Soldiers detain king over communist supporters

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense 'over' turns a word on its head, so the communist word runs right to left
detaining someone keeps them held within, so the soldiers enclose the rest

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers
R for Rex, Latin for king
red is the traditional label for a communist

explanation.surface: Troops arrest a king who is backed by communists.
explanation.walkthrough: GIs, the soldiers, wrap round R followed by the reversed RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Girders are steel or iron beams that bear the load of a structure, so they are supporters.

clue.text: Engineers uranium inside remains?

indicators.note: to engineer something in is to contrive to fit it there, and 'inside' says where it goes

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
to reside is to remain or stay in a place

explanation.surface: Nuclear engineers find uranium within what is left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineers' looks like the RE abbreviation, but here it is a verb: the clue tells you to work uranium into a verb meaning remains. Read whole, it describes spent nuclear fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is what is left behind after a process, such as spent nuclear fuel still containing uranium, so it is the remains.

clue.text: You ignoramus! Her reckless budget ends in disaster

definitions.text: You ignoramus! Her reckless budget ends in disaster

indicators.note: only the closing letter of each of the preceding words is kept
a disaster leaves things in chaos, so the kept letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: final letter
final letter
final letter
final letter
final letter

explanation.surface: An exasperated voter scolds a politician whose rash budget ended in catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022; her government's unfunded mini-budget crashed the markets and she resigned after 49 days.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the former Prime Minister whose reckless 2022 mini-budget ended her premiership in disaster.

clue.text: Thinks about fireman’s red – is no Chippendale revealed?

indicators.note: a Chippendale strips to reveal himself, and here the answer is exposed inside a run of clue words
turning about means facing the other way, so the hidden run reads right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling these words

explanation.surface: A fireman in red wonders whether a male stripper will show himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chippendales are a male striptease troupe, and firemen are a classic costume; the hidden letters run backwards across the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to think over, so 'considers' is a synonym for the verb in its third-person form.

clue.text: Social worker first punches intelligent support

indicators.note: a punch drives in, so the worker letters are knocked into the word for intelligent

blocks.note: the ant is a social insect and a worker ant toils for the colony
I is the Roman numeral one, and first is number one
clever means intelligent

explanation.surface: A social worker is the first to throw punches at a clever person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a job in care, but an ant is the social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam fixed at one end that holds up a balcony or bridge, so it is a support.

clue.text: Deferral of South American allowance

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for South
US for American
a pension is a regular allowance paid in retirement

explanation.surface: A US citizen's retirement payment is put on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase but splits into two short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension is a temporary halt or postponement, so it is a deferral.

clue.text: Joining record set to be broken following European investment opportunities

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so these three letters come back in another order
coming after something puts it behind, so the European abbreviation goes at the front

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
merging means joining together
to mark is to record, as in marking down a score
the three letters of set, reordered

explanation.surface: An athlete about to break a newly set record follows a European rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following European' puts E at the front: the European comes first and everything else follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerging markets are developing economies that investors see as growth prospects, hence investment opportunities.

clue.text: One’s unhappy breaking leg outside in dance movement

indicators.note: a broken limb is out of shape, so the leg letters are rearranged
these letters go round the outside of the unhappy phrase

blocks.note: the letters of leg in a new order
one's becomes I'S, unhappy is SAD

explanation.surface: A dancer is miserable after breaking a leg out on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking a leg' is the theatrical good-luck phrase, here taken literally as a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissade is a gliding step in ballet, so it is a dance movement.

clue.text: Shutting in criminal, maybe in top of gaol

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order
the top of a down word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of gaol

explanation.surface: A criminal is locked up, perhaps in the upper wing of a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To embay is to enclose in a bay or recess, so embaying is shutting something in.

clue.text: Trial by fire axed to protect independent witness

indicators.note: to axe something is to hack at it, so the fire letters are chopped and rearranged
protecting something means surrounding it, so the letters close round the independent

blocks.note: a test is a trial
I is the abbreviation for independent
the letters of fire in a new order

explanation.surface: A trial by fire is cancelled to shield a neutral witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial by fire' is an idiom for a harsh ordeal; here the phrase splits into its pieces, with 'by' setting the trial beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A testifier is someone who gives evidence, typically under oath in court, so it is a witness.

clue.text: Remained sober as instructed

indicators.note: instructions are often given by voice, so the word for sober is to be heard

blocks.note: staid means sober and serious

explanation.surface: Someone stayed off the drink, just as they had been told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sober' suggests not drinking, but here it means serious or sedate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain in one place, so the past tense matches 'remained'.

clue.text: College fellow left out of story in telegram

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so the fellow letter is dropped from the story

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for college
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a fable is a moral story

explanation.surface: A college fellow is omitted from a story told by telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College fellow' reads as one academic, but it gives two separate abbreviations, and only the second is cut from the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is an old word for a telegram, a message sent by telegraph wire.

clue.text: Bishop leaves drinks after church in good health

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they are gone, so the bishop letter departs from the drinks
this places the drinks piece behind the church piece

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
beers are drinks
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop leaves the drinks after the church service, still in fine fettle.
explanation.walkthrough: B for bishop comes from chess notation; the church abbreviation goes first because the drinks come after it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Good health' and 'cheers' are both toasts said when raising a glass.

clue.text: I don’t know the answer to strikes – make void?

indicators.note: a void thing is empty, so this word loses its insides and only its outer pair stays

blocks.note: beats means strikes
the outer letters of make

explanation.surface: Asked about the strikes, someone says they have no idea whether to cancel them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make void' looks like a phrase meaning annul, but it says to empty the word make.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Beats me' is an informal idiom meaning I have no idea, said when stumped by a question.

clue.text: West starting to break up broadcast

blocks.note: Mae West was the American film star
the opening letter of break

explanation.walkthrough: 'West' suggests a compass point, but it is the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam a programme is to transmit it by radio waves, so it is a synonym for broadcast.

clue.text: Stained fabrics in draw starting to discolour, of course

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: a tie is a drawn match
the opening letter of discolour
'of course' is an emphatic yes

explanation.surface: Fabrics in a drawer begin to fade, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' reads like a verb, but a draw is a tied match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dyes are fabrics patterned by tying them before dyeing, so they are deliberately stained cloths.

clue.text: Katy Perry showing character

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two names

explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a type is a single letter or character, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Change the last word down

blocks.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: Someone alters the final word in a down clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a crossword direction but simply gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to alter or correct it, so it is a synonym for change.

clue.text: Language earns poet bucks

indicators.note: a horse that bucks throws things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet makes money from the use of language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' looks like dollars, fitting 'earns', but it is the verb.
